verdict.rationale: Runpod documents its own storage controls. Network volumes are persistent storage that keeps data when compute is terminated. Users can manage files on those volumes through an S3-compatible API, and manage Pods and network volumes through the CLI, including terminating Pods. This gives users some control over where data persists and the ability to manage it. However, the evidence never explicitly describes deletion guarantees, retention policies, or data-erasure behavior. missing for 10: explicit documented deletion/erasure of volumes and data, configurable retention periods or policies, guarantees about data wiping after Pod termination, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can control data retention and deletion

citations.quote: Network volumes provide persistent storage that exists independently of your compute resources. Data is retained when terminate or scale to zero.
This allows you to manage files on your network volumes without launching a Pod, reducing cost and operational friction.
You can manage Pods, Serverless endpoints, templates, network volumes, and models
Create, start, stop, and terminate Pods using the Runpod console or CLI.
